On Rule Note
D002 Numbers with dots, day first: 01.11.2022 · [3.28.5] also with spaces: 20. 01. 2009
D003 Numbers with slashes: 1/11/2022 – a number over 12 decides; otherwise the Discogs release country (US: month/day, elsewhere day/month), with a note and the other reading to choose

D007 Periods across months or years: March 1 to April 2, 1998 · December 2003 to January 2004 · September and October 2026 · between 1997 and 1998 · 1997/98
D008 Month and year: November 2022 · Nov 2022
D009 Seasons give the year: Spring 1998 → 1998
D010 A year alone: 1998
D011 Decades ("late 1970s", "the 70s") cannot be given as a MusicBrainz date and are left out

D013 Several days: June 23 and 24, 2025 · 23 and 25 June 2025 · 23. und 24. Juni 2025 · June 16/17 2018 · [3.28.5] 19 & 20. 01. 2009 · 19./20.01.2009 – consecutive days give one period (2025-06-23 – 2025-06-24, can be split into single dates), other days give several dates and so several rows – (3.31.2) also days with commas only, right before the year ("November 7, 8, 2016", "7, 8, 9 November 2016", "7., 8. November 2016")

D014 Recording dates as a period or separate days within one year: the pool also gets what they have in common – the month (2001-01-20 – 2001-01-25 → 2001-01) or the year (2012-03-01 – 2012-09-30 → 2012); different years give nothing

D022 Performance on several days ("December 11 & 12, 2015", "2012-03-01 – 2012-09-30") from the notes: the column Performance of the date matrix gets what they have in common at once (D014) – the month (2015-12) or the year (2012); across years the period stays. The period and the single days stay in the pool, to be used instead (3.32.0)

D015 ℗ / © wins: keywords count only as whole words ("Fuzzoramarecords", "… Records" are names), capitalised keywords after a ℗ / © sign belong to a name ("℗ Fuzzorama Recordings 2005"), and "©©" (often a typo for ℗ ©) counts as ℗ and ©
D016 A year right after a title in quotation marks – “Madison” 1988 by Albert Irvin (a painting on the cover) – is no date of the release (3.21.0)
D017 Year, month name, day: 1973 October 19 · 1973, Oct. 19th (3.28.5)
D018 A year of a release or issue is no date of the credits and is left out: "originally issued on LP in 1974", "Released 2003", "veröffentlicht 1999" (3.28.5)
D019 The word naming the group of a date is looked for in its own sentence only ("Mixed May 2001. Released 2003." – 2003 is no mix date); a line ending in ":" counts as part of the next one (3.28.5)

D021 A list of dates after one word naming their group ("recorded … on May 27, 2016 (Disc 1), May 26, 2016 (Disc 2) and December 11 & 12, 2015 (Disc 3)") gives the group to each; a medium in brackets right after a date ("(Disc 2)", "(CD 2)") is the track group of that date (3.30.8)

D020 Words naming groups joined by "and", "&" or commas give the date to each group: "Mixed and mastered by X in March 2026" → Mix and Mastering, "Recorded, mixed and mastered 2001" → Performance, Mix and Mastering (3.28.5)

D023 Dates in the titles of the tracks ("March 23, 2004 (Set 1)", "March 23, 2004 (Set 2)"): each date with a day goes into the date pool, the tracks with that date into the track pool ("March 23, 2004 · 1–2") and, as a suggestion, under Performance into the date matrix ("Apply" as usual); "(Set 1)" is no part of the date. Off until switched on (3.31.7)

S015 Track groups: a date whose sentence names tracks ("Tracks 1 to 5 recorded …", "tracks 6, 8 and 10", "A1 to A3", "side B", "CD2, tracks 1–5", "Disc 2" for the whole medium) goes into the date matrix with that track group and only onto those tracks; rows covering more tracks are split, rows with a date of their own stay tracksInText, applyMatrixColumn, applyDateToTracks (date dropped onto a row)
S016 A studio of "Companies, etc." named in the same sentence gets exactly these tracks and this date; other studios are left alone by that date studiosInText, applyMatrixColumn
S017 A Discogs spelling that differs from the MusicBrainz instrument only in spaces or hyphens is no role credit ("Flugel Horn" → flugelhorn, "Hand Claps" → handclaps) wordingCredit
S018 An engineer with several tasks is one role per task: "Engineer [Mix, Recording]" → mix and recording (each with the other details, e.g. "Assistant") splitEngineerTasks

S020 Music and lyrics in one credit (R098): new works of these tracks get the work type "Song" (the default for all new works when the credit is for the whole release); a type chosen by hand stays applySongDefault

S021 "live" is preselected on new links recording → work (a new work, or a work linked here) when the release group is marked Live in MusicBrainz, Discogs calls the release live (format, "recorded live" in the notes), or the track title says so ("(live)", "[live]", "(live at …)", "– live"), or a "Live Recording By" credit names the track (the whole release without track list); unticking takes it back. Links that exist in MusicBrainz keep their attributes: "live" is only offered there ("li?") applyLiveDefault, linkAttrsOf, liveHint

S022 Track lists in the Discogs notes ("XYZ Publishing (1, 4, 6)", "Published by X (tracks 1–3)", "Written by Y (2, 5)", "Tracks 1, 4 & 6 published by Z"): a track group in the pool; when the name is an entry of the dashboard (compared generously: case, accents, spaces, hyphens, punctuation, "&"/"and", Ltd./GmbH/Inc. …, one typo; as a last step without generic words like Publishing, Music, Verlag – marked "similar"), its work-level roles get these tracks as a suggestion (dashed, ✓ keeps, × takes out), ahead of the personal publisher evidence (S014). Credits Discogs gives on these tracks already are left alone; unknown names only give the track group notesTrackCredits, matchEntry, applyNotesTrackCredits

S023 A track group dropped onto the works matrix: onto an attribute in the head of the track column (the links of these tracks get it, the others lose it), onto a role of a column (that role only for the works of these tracks) or onto a column head (all its roles); with Shift added instead. Relationships and attributes already in MusicBrainz stay dropTracksOnMatrix

S024 "Commissioned By" (R099, C037) without a track list: "commissioned" is suggested on all works (dashed, yellow; ✓ keeps it, × takes it out, it is staged like the others). With a track list it is set on the works of those tracks suggestCommissioned

S019 Details that only repeat the role in another word form are no role credit: "Mixed By [Mixing]", "Mastered By [Mastering]", "Music By [All Music By]", "Recorded By [Recording]"; "[Cover Photo]" stays repeatedDetails

S026 A credit for a medium the MusicBrainz release does not have ("Vinyl LP mastering", "Mastered By [Vinyl]", "Lacquer Cut By" on a release of Digital Media) is no row: it is listed as left out on purpose, with the reason. "Vinyl LP mastering and digital mastering by X" keeps the digital mastering. A medium word of a text that fits the release is no role credit (3.21.4) loadRelease, suppRow, mediumOfRow (MEDIUM_WORDS)

S027 Tracks named by their titles in a text (T036: "Piano in ‘A' and 'B' is a contribution by X", "Guitar on “Song”: Y"): each title is looked for among the tracks of the source (a pasted text: MusicBrainz's, Bandcamp: the album's) – case, accents and punctuation do not count, one letter more, less or other is allowed; a title not found is shown as "not matched", its tracks are chosen by hand (3.22.0) titleScope, tracksByTitles (TEXT_TITLE_SCOPE)

S028 An area of a text ("Recorded by X in Xixon, Asturies, Spain", T037) is an entry of the kind "Area" with the larger areas after it; MusicBrainz is searched with its other names too ("Xixon" finds Gijón with the alias "Xixón") – only suggested, nothing assigned; there is no "Create" (areas are added by MusicBrainz's area editors). Its type: recorded in, mixed in (recording) or mastered in (release) (3.22.0); produced in, remixed in, engineered in, and the area each suggestion is part of, read from MusicBrainz ("City, Asturias"; 3.22.2) suggestByName, groupKindOf, matchHtmlInner (C038 …)

S029 A Bandcamp album on another account's page – mostly a label's ("Grabaciones Autobombo" with an album of Yunclas): the name of the page (its "data-band", else "og:site_name") is not the album's artist (case, accents and "The" do not count; "Jane Roe & Friends" on Jane Roe's page is her own) – the page is no link of the artist, he is searched by name, the entry says whose page it is and names MusicBrainz's label with that page. People not found through their own link (Discogs, Bandcamp) get the same-named MusicBrainz entries as suggestions; an artist of the release's artist credit with that name comes first, marked "release artist" – only suggested (3.22.1) bandPageName, ownPage, linkBand, bandPageInfo, suggestByName

S030 Every import compares the tracks of the source with those of the MusicBrainz release: their number and their titles position by position (T038: case, accents, punctuation, notes in brackets, "feat. …" and small words do not count; a title fits when it has the same words, is in the other, is one letter off or shares more than half of the words of the shorter one; different numbers never). Different numbers or less than 80 % fitting titles: a yellow warning with what differs (the titles in the message). In the dialog of several linked releases each gets it, and the most data is chosen among those whose tracks fit (3.24.1) trackFit, titlesFit, loadRelease, chooseLink (TITLE_SMALL_WORDS)

S031 A name that differs from MusicBrainz's only in its case ("Voices Of Wonder" for Voices of Wonder, "VALFAR" for Valfar) gets no "credited as": MusicBrainz's spelling is used, for the name at the source and for a Discogs "credited as" (ANV). Typed in by hand, it stays (3.28.2) sourceCreditFor, syncSourceCredits

S032 A role in Norwegian, Swedish or Danish (T039) – in a Discogs bracket that names the role itself ("Mixed By [Miksa Av]", "Graphics [Grafisk Utforming]", "Producer [Produsert Av]", "Mastered By [Mastering Av]") or as the role of a text ("Miksa av: X") – is a translation: mapped as its English term, no role credit (3.28.2) mapRole, repeatedDetails, roleCreditFor (ROLE_TERMS)

S033 The tasks of an artwork credit joined by "and" ("Artwork [Logo Og Kunst]" – Norwegian for logo and art –, "Logo og kunst: X", "Logo and Art") each become their own role as Discogs writes it in English (T040): design with the credit "logo" and artwork with the credit "art". Only when every part is such a task; the row says the role as written at the source (3.28.2). Tasks of one MusicBrainz type stay one row of that type, credited with the tasks in English: "Artwork [Design And Layout]" → design "design and layout" (3.28.4) splitArtTasks, parseRoles, groupCredits (ART_TASKS)
S034 The kind of a voice is written in lower case in its role credit ("Vocals [Screams]" → screams, "Vocals [Clean]" → clean), also words MusicBrainz does not know (3.28.2) roleCreditFor, caseCredit

S035 An instrument MusicBrainz does not have under its whole name (two to four words) is looked for by its last word ("wood flutes" → flute, after every other candidate); found only that way, the whole wording is its role credit, in lower case ("wood flutes"). In texts not for a name-like phrase ("John Bass") (3.28.2) instrumentCandidates, headNounCands, byHeadNoun, roleCreditFor

S036 A name from a text or Bandcamp linked to a MusicBrainz entry is credited as written there ("K.M." for the artist it is linked to), unless it is the same or differs only in its case (S031); not a placeholder ("the band"), not a supplement. Typed in by hand, it stays (3.28.4) syncSourceCredits, sourceCreditFor

S037 The design of a part of the package keeps its whole name as role credit: "Cover Design", "Cover Design By", "Design [Cover]", "Cover [Design]", "Artwork [Cover Design]" → design credited "cover design"; also sleeve, booklet, package, packaging, digipak, inlay, insert (3.28.4) roleRules (design rule R062, DESIGN_PARTS)

S038 Prose with names and their roles in brackets after "by": "A chronicle of rabid deeds, dutifully unearthed … by K.M. (sounds, words) & E. (voice)" → K.M. performer and lyricist, E. vocals – the words before "by" are no role, the brackets are (T041, or roles of the register: "(guitar, vocals)"); every name needs a bracket (3.29.0) TEXT.parse (namesWithRoles, PROSE_ROLE_WORDS)

S039 Verbs joined before "at" each give the place: "Mixed and mastered at TQA.HQ (July 2026)" → mixed at and mastered at TQA.HQ; a date in brackets after the place is no part of it (3.29.0) TEXT.parse (place, placeOf)

S040 A list of kinds before a shared instrument also with commas only ("Tenor, alto, soprano saxophones", "Tenor / alto / soprano saxophones") – each kind gets the instrument, in the singular when the list ends in the plural (tenor saxophone, alto saxophone, soprano saxophone) (3.29.0) TEXT.parse (splitRoles, INSTRUMENT_MODIFIER)

S041 The members of the band: "Vision Fortune are AC Williams, Alex Townend and Andres Ayerbe" – the release's artist (or "the band", "we") before "are", "is", "consists of" – each name a performer on all tracks, as a suggestion (names with capitals only); also from the "about" text of Bandcamp, which otherwise gives only places (3.30.7, T043) TEXT.parse (TEXT_MEMBERS, isTheBand; BANDCAMP.toRelease)

S042 Discogs notes: the places they name ("All music recorded … at Orange Music Sound Studios in West Orange, New Jersey", "mastered … at Turtle Tone Studio in New York City") are added, read like a pasted text – unless Discogs lists the place with that role already; listed with another role, Discogs's entry gets it (3.30.8) addNotesCompanies (TEXT.parse of the notes)

S043 Publishers below a heading ("[Publishers & Rights Societies]", "Publishers:", "Publishing (all BMI):") – one per line with its rights society and tracks ("FlizmoMusic-BMI : tracks 2, 4, 5"; outside a block a line with a society after the name too): publishing on those tracks; the society (T045) is the release's rights society, once each, also from "Published by X (BMI)" and a line of societies only ("BIEM/GEMA"). In the Discogs notes the tracks go onto Discogs's publisher of that name (also written together or with a number as a word, T046) as suggestions; publishers and societies not found through their link are searched by name (3.31.0) TEXT.parse (PUBLISHER_HEAD, SOCIETY_AFTER_NAME, SOCIETY_LINE), addNotesCompanies, resolveArtists

S044 A person as publisher: a publisher with the name of a person of the dashboard ("Published By – Tomas Fujiwara", "Tomas Fujiwara-BMI : tracks 1, 6, 8") is no company – its publishing becomes a role of the person (artist–work "publishing", MusicBrainz's "published / publisher"), in the person's column of the works matrix next to writer or composer; the company entry is left out, the row says that Discogs lists it as a company; without tracks of its own, the works the person writes are suggested (3.31.5; 3.31.0–3.31.4: a part of the person's column with a label of its own) mergePersonPublishers, computePublisherEvidence, roleCell

S048 A publisher with the name of a person and no entry of the dashboard (two to four words with capitals, no word of a company such as "Music", "Publishing", "Songs", no legal form – T044): MusicBrainz's artists of that name are offered first and "Create artist …"; when MusicBrainz has an artist of exactly that name, a label of that name only when its type is "Publisher", and no "Create label …" (otherwise both, as the name may be a company's: "Pub House") (3.31.5) personLikeName, suggestByName, matchHtmlInner, startCompanyCreate

S045 A rights society after the name of a writer ("Composed by Tomas Fujiwara (BMI)", "Music: Jane Doe-ASCAP", "Lyrics by Ann Poe / GEMA" – composer, lyricist, writer, arranger, librettist, translator): the society is the release's rights society (once each, T045), the name is taken without it. In pasted texts, Bandcamp credits and the Discogs notes (3.32.0) TEXT.parse (WRITER_WORDS_IN, stripWriterSocieties)

S046 Performers on tracks, instruments for the release: a person credited "Performer" on some tracks only and with instruments or voices for the whole release only ("Performer – Barry Guy" on 4-3 and 4-5, "Bass – Barry Guy" for the release) gets the instruments on the tracks of the "Performer" credits, across all media; the "performer" rows go (they would say the same). Someone without an instrument keeps "performer"; instruments without a "Performer" credit stay on all tracks. Who plays which of several instruments where, Discogs does not say: all of them on all of these tracks. Off until switched on (3.31.8) applyPerformerTracks

S047 The kind of engineer said twice: "Engineer [Recording Engineer]" is read as "Engineer [Recording]" – recording without role credit; "[Mix Engineer]" mix, "[Mastering Engineer]" mastering, "[Assistant Engineer]" engineer with "assistant", "[Sound Engineer]" sound engineer (3.31.3) mapRoleInner

S049 Credits in Bandcamp's "about" text: every credit line of it is read like those of the credits field ("Music and cover art by j4vaman" → composer, cover art) – also when the credits field has credits; prose gives nothing, its lines are not listed as not recognized; the rows say "from the about text" and go with "Leave out the about text". Before only its places and areas, the members of the band (S041) and the liner notes. Switch also in ⚙ Settings → Texts BANDCAMP.toRelease (aboutRes), linerNotes, artistSignature

S050 Typos in role words: a part of a text that gives nothing is read again with each unknown word of five letters or more that is one letter off a role word (T048) – a letter swapped, missing, too many or wrong – read as that word, when the role is known then ("Muisc and cover art by X" → Music By, cover art); only role words, never names; the row says "Read as “Music” (written “Muisc”)". All texts (pasted, Bandcamp, Discogs notes); switch also in ⚙ Settings → Texts TEXT.parse (typoMode, readRole), fixRoleTypo, roleVocab, roleCell

S051 Instruments and the name they are played by: lines that are only instruments or voices (one or several each, empty lines between them), then a line "are played, mixed and produced by X" (also "played by X", "All instruments played by X"): each instrument a row of X, the other verbs roles of their own ("Mixed By", "Produced By"), "played" none (T049). In one line too: "Electric guitar, drums and piano are played by X", "X plays guitar, bass and drums". Lines without an instrument before the first one are read as usual; words that are no instrument MusicBrainz knows are listed as not recognized. Words like "are", "is", "were" before a verb are never a part of the role (T050: "are played by X" is "Played By", before "Played By [Are]") TEXT.parse (roleBlock, readBlock, linkOf, chainOf, playedList, PLAYS_LIST)

S052 Role credits and tasks in lower case, proper names keep their capitals: only the proper names of MusicBrainz's instruments ("Hammond", "Rhodes") and models with digits ("TR-808") stay as written. So the role credit of "other instruments" for a word MusicBrainz does not know ("Chaims" → chaims, "Sticks-And-Stones" → sticks-and-stones), the task of miscellaneous support and of other text attributes ("Tour Manager" → tour manager) and the suggestions of the role credit field, which are written like the role credit (S011; before: as written on Discogs). From 3.34.28 also the words of Discogs brackets and wordings MusicBrainz does not know ("Guitar [Gibson Les Paul]" → Gibson les paul) and the proper names of the register keep theirs (T052: "Buddha machine"); a word of an unknown role or instrument or of a bracket written small says so at the row – "Written small – unknown to MusicBrainz: Les → les · keep “Les” · always write “Les”" (always: into T052). Off: tasks all in lower case, "other instruments" credited as written and the brackets as S011 says, as before lowerCredit, lowerWord, roleCreditFor, guessCredit, guessTask, roleCreditOptions (creditCasing), caseNoteHtml, caseKeep, caseAlways

S025 An instrument or voice in German, Spanish or French (T034: "Schlagzeug", "batería", "batterie") is mapped as its English term and gets no role credit – it is a translation, MusicBrainz's own name is used ("Flügel" → grand piano, "batterie" → drums (drum set), not credited "drums"; 3.21.2) mapRole, roleCreditFor (FOREIGN_TERMS)

S011 Artwork role credits are in lower case; instrument models keep their capitals ("Fender Rhodes"); from 3.34.28 with S052 only proper names (MusicBrainz's and T052) and models with digits roleCreditFor, caseCredit (ART_TYPES, GENERIC_WORDS)

T004 "Companies, etc." roles → MusicBrainz types for labels, places, areas (3.22.0) and artists (rules C001 …) COMPANY_ROLES
T005 Details that stand for a MusicBrainz checkbox or attribute ("Additional Musicians" → additional, "Remaster" → re) (S002) DETAIL_FLAGS
T006 Words that only name the kind of relationship and are no role credit ("Music By" = composer, "Engineer [Mix]" = mix) WORDING_SYNONYMS
T007 Role credits kept when MusicBrainz names the instrument differently ("Drums" → drums (drum set), credited "drums") FIXED_ROLE_CREDITS

T009 Texts: separators between names, between roles, and before a shared instrument word ("tenor & soprano sax") TEXT_NAME_SEP, TEXT_ROLE_SEP, TEXT_AND_SEP

T011 Texts: words that name a kind of an instrument and share its noun ("tenor & soprano sax" → tenor and soprano saxophone) INSTRUMENT_MODIFIER

T013 Texts: roles that name a company (published by, recorded at, ℗ / ©); other "… by" are people TEXT_COMPANY_RE
T014 Dates: month names (English, German, Spanish, French) and ordinal words (D004, D005) MONTH_NAMES, ORDINALS, TEXT_MONTHS
T015 Dates: words near a date that name its date group ("recorded", "mixed", "mastered", "℗") (D015) DATE_HINTS
T016 Date groups: the MusicBrainz relationships that share a column of the date matrix DATE_GROUPS
T017 Track titles that say "live": "(Live)", "(Live at …)", "[Live]", "– Live" (S021) LIVE_TITLE
T018 Roles named with a track list in the notes ("XYZ Publishing (1, 4, 6)", "Written by Y (2, 5)") (S022) NOTE_ROLES
T019 Texts: what follows "at" without being a place ("at the same time", "at last", "at night", "at the end of …") NOT_A_PLACE
T020 Texts: a time after a name is cut off ("… by X in October 2026" → X; the date goes into the pool) TEXT_TIME_AFTER_NAME
T021 Texts: words before a verb that only say what was done ("Music played and recorded by X" → played by, recorded by) TEXT_WHAT_WORDS
T022 Texts: roles named before a verb of making ("Music and artwork of this release were entirely created by …") TEXT_MADE_BY
T023 Texts: a person without a name after "by" ("a human", "the band", "himself") – the release artist is suggested PLACEHOLDER_WHO
T024 Texts: lines that only name the label ("An X release.", "Released on X") are left out; ℗ / © lines stay credits TEXT_LABEL_LINE
T025 Texts: words that are no part of a name after a role at the start of a line ("Photography Tom Barrett") TEXT_NOT_NAME
T026 Works of the artists: special purpose artists are not compared (Various Artists, [unknown] …; any name entirely in [square brackets] too) SPECIAL_ARTISTS
T027 Bandcamp (3.17.2): liner notes below the "about" text – a first word that makes the line no name ("Special Thanks"), and particles inside a name ("Jan van Roe") LINER_NOT_NAME, LINER_PARTICLE
T028 Texts (3.17.3): words for the distribution of a release ("Distribution - !K7", "Distributor: X", "Vertrieb: X") – read as "Distributed By" (C006) TEXT_DISTRIBUTION

T029 Texts (3.21.0): a line with several sentences ("Graphic design: X. Text: Y. Produced by Z.") is read sentence by sentence – a period after these words, after an initial ("J. Smith") or before a small letter ends no sentence TEXT_ABBREV

T030 Texts (3.21.0): lines left out on purpose – thanks ("Thanks to …", "Danke an …"), endorsements ("X plays exclusively on Y bass strings"), "appears courtesy of …", [3.30.8] the package ("Including a 52 p. booklet."); listed apart from the lines not recognized TEXT_IGNORE_LINE, TEXT_PACKAGE

T031 Texts (3.21.0): after a name "courtesy of …" ("by kind permission of …") is no name; a title in quotation marks with its year before "by" ("Cover art: “Madison” 1988 by X") is no part of the role TEXT_COURTESY, TEXT_QUOTED_TITLE

T032 Texts (3.21.0): web addresses are never part of a name; a profile on these sites after a name becomes a link of the entry (MusicBrainz is asked for it, "Create artist" fills it in); Linktree, e-mail and any other address are left out, as is a line of only addresses ("Contact: …"). 3.21.3: artist pages of streaming services (Spotify, Apple Music, Deezer, Tidal, YouTube Music, Qobuz, Amazon Music) only for "Create artist" (STREAM_URL), profiles after a label or place for "Create label/place"; shown at the entry only with the setting WEB_ADDRESS, SOCIAL_HOSTS, WEB_LABEL

T034 Texts (3.21.2): instruments and voices in German, Spanish and French, each spelling with its language (word@de, word@es,fr; the search field filters "@de") → the English term the register maps; a translation gets no role credit (S025), accents do not count FOREIGN_TERMS, foldWord

T035 Texts and all sources (3.21.4): words for a medium in a role ("Vinyl LP mastering", "Mastered for vinyl", "Mastering [Vinyl]", "(CD)", "Lacquer Cut") and the kinds of MusicBrainz media formats – a credit for a medium the release does not have is left out (S026) MEDIUM_WORDS, mediumKindOf, formatKind

T036 Texts (3.22.0): tracks named by their titles in quotation marks after a role and "in", "on" ("Piano in ‘A' and 'B'", "Guitar on “Song”"; the marks may be mixed) – the tracks of these titles (S027); "is a contribution", "was played", "were performed" before "by" leave the role TEXT_TITLE_SCOPE, TEXT_CONTRIBUTION

T037 Texts (3.22.0): an area after a name ("Recorded by X in Xixon, Asturies, Spain") or a verb ("Recorded in Berlin", "Mixed live in Paris") – words with capitals (particles between them: "Frankfurt am Main", "Rio de Janeiro"), up to four parts, no number, month or season, none of these words first; a time after it ("in the spring, 2017") is left out. Only for recorded, mixed, mastered and (3.22.2) produced, remixed, engineered (C038 – C043, S028) areaOf, TEXT_AREA_PARTICLE, TEXT_NOT_AREA

T038 Track titles compared with MusicBrainz's (3.24.1, S030): small words of English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese and Dutch are left out ("The Song of the Sea" = "Song of Sea"), so are notes in brackets ("(Remastered)", "[Live]", "(feat. X)") TITLE_SMALL_WORDS, TITLE_NOTE, titleWordsOf

T041 Texts (3.29.0): role words in brackets after a name in prose (S038) and the role each stands for ("sounds" → performer (3.30.6: "Sounds", R104, the dashboard asks for effects – Q008), "words" → lyricist, "voice" → vocals; 3.29.1: "noises" → effects credited "noises", "electronics" → electronic instruments credited "electronics", "field recordings" → field recordist) PROSE_ROLE_WORDS

T042 Texts (3.29.0): words of prose around a credit that are left out – a verb before "by" ("Cover artwork channeled by X", "Logo carved by …") and words before the name ("… by the guided hand of BMS Illustration") PROSE_FILLER_VERB, PROSE_FILLER_BEFORE_NAME

T043 Texts (3.30.7): the members of a band – the release's artist (or the band named by itself: "the band", "the trio", "we") before "are", "is", "consists of" …, then the names (S041) TEXT_MEMBERS, TEXT_BAND_SELF

T039 All sources (3.28.2): roles in Norwegian, Swedish and Danish, each spelling with its language (word@no, word@sv, word@da; the search field filters "@no") → the English role the register maps; in a Discogs bracket or as a role of a text, a translation gets no role credit (S032) ROLE_TERMS, ROLE_INDEX, foldWord
T040 All sources (3.28.2): the tasks of an artwork credit that "and" (og, och, und, et, y, &, +) joins, with the role each becomes (S033) ART_TASKS, ART_TASK_INDEX, splitArtTasks

T044 All sources (3.30.9): the legal form at the end of a company's name (Oy, AB, AS, ApS, Ltd, GmbH, KG, Inc., LLC, Corp., S.A., S.L., S.r.l., B.V., N.V., Pty …): a name without a link is also searched without it – "TUM Records Oy" offers TUM Records Oy and TUM Records COMPANY_FORM, withoutCompanyForm, suggestByName

T045 All sources (3.31.0): rights societies, as MusicBrainz names them (labels of the type Rights Society; on the release level, C032) – after a publisher's name ("-BMI", "(ASCAP)", "/ GEMA"), in a line of their own ("BIEM/GEMA"); the heading of a block of publishers (S043) RIGHTS_SOCIETIES, PUBLISHER_HEAD, SOCIETY_AFTER_NAME, SOCIETY_LINE

T046 All sources (3.31.0): a company's name written together ("FlizmoMusic", "4WordSeaMusic", "Fourwordseamusic") – searched in MusicBrainz written apart too and with a number as a word ("Flizmo Music", "4 Word Sea Music", "Four Word Sea Music", "Fourwordsea Music"); compared so too (S043), offered as similar apartNames, digitWords, sameCompanyName, suggestByName

T047 Texts (3.32.5): a date right after a place ("El Studio in San Francisco on September 3rd and 4th 2016", "… in September 2016", "… on 2016-09-03") is cut off before the place is read; the area before it stays. (3.34.18) Also a date with its year first without a preposition ("…, Rotterdam 2024 January - July", D024) PLACE_DATE_TAIL, placeOf
T048 Texts (3.32.5): the words of roles a typo is read as (S050: "Muisc" → "Music"); on MusicBrainz also the words of its relationship types and attributes ROLE_WORDS, roleVocab, fixRoleTypo

T051 Texts (3.34.18): a name after "in" with a word of places (studio, hall, church, club, theatre …) and a word in capitals besides it is a place, not an area – "Recorded in Guruguru Brain studio, Rotterdam, 2024 January - July" gives the place Guruguru Brain studio (recorded at) with its area Rotterdam; "Recorded in Berlin" stays an area TEXT_PLACE_WORDS, placeIn

T052 Proper names in role credits (3.34.28): words that keep their capitals although MusicBrainz's instruments do not hold them ("Buddha machine", makes such as Fender, Moog, Wurlitzer; peoples such as Irish, Tibetan) – every other word MusicBrainz does not know is written small (S052). From 3.35.2 also names of several words ("Gibson Les Paul", "Les Paul"): only as a whole in this spelling, a "les" elsewhere stays small.
